questions.knowledge_point: Finding Two Scalar Factors in a Linear Combination
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069110/assets/41a40c03043152177c5bf6d7f56b51c09e57352480599b508d376018d87de1b3.png)

Consider the picture above. Given that $c=\lambda a+\mu b$, find $\lambda $ and $\mu .$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069110/assets/ccc52cbcbf17db97ad3849f157b5d6ab3e10f59846e2cd4b75507fc0a37c3c98.png)

In $△OAC$ shown above, we have:

- $OA=3|a|$

- $\overset{\to }{OA}$ and $a$ have opposite directions

Hence, $\overset{\to }{OA}=-3a.$

Similarly:

- $AC=2|b|$

- $\overset{\to }{AC}$ and $b$ have opposite directions

Hence, $\overset{\to }{AC}=-2b.$

Additionally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\overset{\to }{OA}+\overset{\to }{AC} \\  & =-3a-2b.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $c=\lambda a+\mu b=-3a-2b.$ 

Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients, we get:

- $\lambda =-3$ and $\mu =-2$

questions.knowledge_point: Expressing a Vector That Satisfies a Ratio in Terms of Known Vectors
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069110/assets/ba82c6b68026b0f4339c1e4fa01c4b1aa1b7aee74b74176f81bba1c0e1de259f.png)

Consider the diagram above, where $\overset{\to }{OR}=r,$ $\overset{\to }{OS}=s$ and $V$ divides $\overset{―}{RS}$ in the ratio $RV:VS=6:5.$ Find $\overset{\to }{OV}.$
questions.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that

$$
\overset{\to }{OV}=\overset{\to }{OR}+\overset{\to }{RV}.
$$

We're told that $\overset{\to }{OR}=r,$ so we just need to work out $\overset{\to }{RV}.$

First, from $△ORS,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{RS} & =\overset{\to }{RO}+\overset{\to }{OS} \\  & =-\overset{\to }{OR}+\overset{\to }{OS} \\  & =-r+s \\  & =s-r.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $RV:VS=6:5,$ we have

$$
\overset{\to }{RV}=\frac{6}{11}\overset{\to }{RS}=\frac{6}{11}(s-r).
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{OV} & =\overset{\to }{OR}+\overset{\to }{RV} \\  & =r+\frac{6}{11}(s-r) \\  & =\frac{5}{11}r+\frac{6}{11}s.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the diagram above, where $\overset{\to }{OU}=u,$ $\overset{\to }{OV}=v,$ and $W$ divides $\overset{―}{UV}$ in the ratio $UW:WV=9:8.$ Express $\overset{\to }{OW}$ via the vectors $u$ and $v.$

questions.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that

$$
\overset{\to }{OW}=\overset{\to }{OU}+\overset{\to }{UW}.
$$

We're told that $\overset{\to }{OU}=u,$ so we just need to work out $\overset{\to }{UW}.$

First, from $△OUV,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{UV} & =\overset{\to }{UO}+\overset{\to }{OV} \\  & =-\overset{\to }{OU}+\overset{\to }{OV} \\  & =-u+v \\  & =v-u.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $UW:WV=9:8,$ we have

$$
\overset{\to }{UW}=\frac{9}{17}\overset{\to }{UV}=\frac{9}{17}(v-u).
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{OW} & =\overset{\to }{OU}+\overset{\to }{UW} \\  & =u+\frac{9}{17}(v-u) \\  & =\frac{8}{17}u+\frac{9}{17}v.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
To find $\lambda ,$ we want to match the expression

$$
c=\lambda a+3b.
$$

We are given that one of the components is $3b.$ So, we first draw the vector $3b$ from the origin. Then we complete the path to the point $C.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069110/assets/43fdebc1ce180542e3cfdaf3f19e27e7ac869bbc5e37da7380886bd3d817bfb7.png)

Let $P$ be the endpoint of the vector $3b.$ Then

$$
c=\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC}.
$$

In $△OPC,$ we have:

- $PC=|a|$

- $\overset{\to }{PC}$ and $a$ have opposite directions

Hence, $\overset{\to }{PC}=-a.$

Additionally,

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC} \\  & =3b-a.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $c=\lambda a+3b=-a+3b.$

Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients of $a,$ we get:

$$
\lambda =-1
$$
